content: ART4, also known as Ecto-ADP-ribosyltransferase 4, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the ART4 gene. This enzyme is also referred to as CD297, which stands for Cluster of Differentiation 297. The ART4 gene encodes a protein that contains a mono-ADP-ribosylation (ART) motif. While it is classified as a member of the ADP-ribosyltransferase gene family, its enzymatic activity has not been experimentally demonstrated. The protein product of this gene is anchored to the erythrocyte membrane via a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor. This protein is also the site of antigens associated with the Dombrock blood group system. Several allelic variants of ART4 are known, some of which are associated with adverse transfusion reactions. Within the Dombrock blood group system, multiple antigens have been identified. These include DOA, DOJO1, DOA-WL, DODOYA, DOB, DOB-WL, DOB-SH-Q149K, DOB-(WL)-I175N, DOHY1, DOHY2, and DODOMR. To study the function of ART4, model organisms have been utilized. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Art4tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of ART4 gene deletion.
